title: Orchestrator + Runtime Ownership Sketchpad
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working sketch to clarify who owns which responsibilities across the orchestration/control-plane surface and the runtime adapter layer in a multi-region setup. Intention is to be concrete enough for oncall/hand-off, but lightweight: a map + clear decision points, not a full runbook.

Context / constraints (quick recap):
- We operate three logical planes: API edge (ingress/gateway), control-plane (orchestrator, routing policies, rollouts), and data-plane (runtime adapters + serving runtime).
- Customers can be on Hosted, Dedicated, or Private (VPC). Ownership may vary by deployment mode; default below assumes Hosted unless noted.
- Multi-region: prefer regional routing for latency + data locality, with global orchestrator for config/versioning where appropriate.

High-level goals for ownership split:
1) Clear owner for decision points (where policy chooses a variant/resource).
2) Minimal cross-team blast radius for incidents (fail closed vs fail open).
3) Document escalation paths for cross-plane failures.
4) Explicit contract surface (small set of RPCs + expected invariants).

Components (working names):
- Edge Gateway: http/gRPC ingress, TLS termination, WAF, rate limiting.
- API Orchestrator: policy engine for routing (latency/cost/region), rollout controller (canary, A/B), model catalog pointers, regional capacity hints.
- Runtime Adapter (RA): per-provider/regional adapter that translates orchestrator requests into concrete runtime calls (e.g., to Dedicated GPU pool, hosted runtime, or on-prem agent).
- Serving Runtime: the actual model serving process (quantized model, KV cache, batching layer).
- Metadata & Config Store: versioned config for models, routing weights, adapter capability registry.

Ownership proposals (practical):
- Edge Gateway: owned by eng-platform-edge team. Responsible for ingress SLAs, TLS, basic auth and untrusted surface filtering. They do not make model-level routing decisions beyond header-based routing.
- API Orchestrator: owned by eng-platform-orchestrator (control plane). Responsible for policy evaluation, rollout state, and decision telemetry. The orchestrator is also the owner of the model catalog references (logical model versions).
- Runtime Adapters: owned by eng-serving-runtime (with regional stewards in infra teams). Adapters own the translation to runtimes and capability flags (supports-kv-cache, supports-quantized, max-concurrency).
- Serving Runtime: eng-serving-runtime primarily, but Dedicated capacity ops owns reserved pool management and infra-specific scaling/autoscaler hooks.
- Config/Metadata Store: eng-platform-infra (central), but orchestrator is the producer of routing policies; serving runtime reads runtime-capability metadata via adapter registry.

Minimal contract (API surface between orchestrator and adapters):
- EvaluateRoute(context): returns target runtime variant + token-cost-estimate + latency-SLO class.
- StartInvocation(session_id, model_ref, opts): returns invocation_id and initial KV hints.
- StreamTokens(invocation_id, chunk): streaming RPC for responses (server push).
- ReportInvocationComplete(invocation_id, metrics): success/failure, tokens, model-version-hash, latency.
- HealthProbe(): returns {status, capacity_hint, supported_features}.

Who owns what when a request fails? (decision matrix)
- Gateway-level failures (TLS handshake, invalid auth): edge team owns.
- Policy eval failures (orchestrator crashes, schema mismatch): orchestrator owner. If orchestrator is unavailable, default fallback is: 1) if edge sees "sticky-route" header -> forward to last-known region, 2) otherwise route to low-cost fallback runtime (configured by orchestrator previously).
- Adapter translation errors (e.g., protocol mismatch): runtime-adapter owner. Adapters should translate errors into standardized codes the orchestrator understands (see linked artifacts).
- Runtime-level failures (OOM, kernel crash): serving-runtime team + oncall for region-specific infra. Adapter should bubble up capacity status to orchestrator so new requests avoid unhealthy nodes.

SLO / oncall boundaries (proposal):
- Edge: 99.95% request-accept rate, owned by eng-platform-edge.
- Orchestrator: 99.9% policy-eval success under normal load. Orchestrator must degrade gracefully: if internal state unavailable, return a deterministic fallback decision (see above).
- Adapter: 99% translation success and accurate capability reporting. Adapter must expose capacity_hint metric used by orchestrator autoscaler.
- Serving runtime: token-latency SLOs per model-class (p50/p95/p99) — owned by serving-runtime but grade of service is negotiated with Dedicated ops for committed pools.

Operational runes (practical, things to add to runbook):
- How to rotate owner for a component temporarily (oncall shift).
- How to change fallback policy (must go through orchestrator changelog, require canary rollout).
- Emergency rollback: orchestrator supports global "force-fallback" flag controlled by platform infra SRE for 2-hour emergency window.

Ownership matrix (CSV-like lines to copy into a doc/spreadsheet):
component,primary_owner,secondary_owner,notes
Edge Gateway,eng-platform-edge,eng-sre,Ingress + auth + basic routing
API Orchestrator,eng-platform-orchestrator,eng-platform-infra,Policy eval + rollout controller
Runtime Adapter,eng-serving-runtime,platform-region-stewards,Adapter capability & translation
Serving Runtime,eng-serving-runtime,dedicated-ops,Model hosting, batching, KV cache
Config Store,eng-platform-infra,eng-platform-orchestrator,Versioned configs + changelog

Open questions / TODOs (action items):
- Define exact RPC schema (proto) for the orchestrator<->adapter surface. Marcus to draft by 2025-02-09 (follow-up: github PR linked above).
- Determine how Private (VPC) deployments override ownership: recommended approach is that customer infra owns their adapter + runtime for private, with Redwood providing orchestration control-plane only if requested. Need legal/OSS review.
- Decide whether orchestrator should run globally or regionally with cross-region consensus for rollout state. Tradeoffs: global simplifies single source but increases blast radius.
- Add concrete telemetry contract: what fields must adapters report in ReportInvocationComplete for SLO and cost attribution. Priya to prototype JSON schema.

Quick example flow (happy path):
1) Client -> Edge (auth + header)
2) Edge forwards to Orchestrator EvaluateRoute (includes region hint, customer tier, prompt meta)
3) Orchestrator returns runtime_variant=us-west-2-dedicated-v2, invocation_opts={use_kv:true, priority:normal}
4) Edge translates request to Runtime Adapter endpoint for us-west-2 pool and calls StartInvocation -> invocation_id
5) Streaming tokens flow via StreamTokens until complete, adapter calls ReportInvocationComplete
6) Orchestrator records telemetry, adjusts weights if rollout strategy indicates (canary success -> increase weight).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally a sketch — please annotate ownership disputes inline or add comments in the PR.
- If you think a component is missing (eg. a separate "routing-caching" service), add a short note and tag the likely owner.

Recent discussion links / context (Slack threads / PRs):
- slack:#platform-orchestrator thread "regional-fallback-proposal" (Jan 2025)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/87 (decisioning flow sketch)

Sign-off checklist (who needs to approve before we freeze ownership?):
- eng-platform-edge lead (edge)
- eng-platform-orchestrator lead (orchestrator)
- eng-serving-runtime lead (adapters + runtime)
- platform SRE lead (oncall/incident process)

-- end of sketch --

(Notes to self: move this into a small Confluence page once owners agree; keep this file as the working sketch for now.)
